clue.text: With enough business money for bill, one escapes suspension from work

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a business
a tab is a bill run up at a bar

indicators.note: one thing escaping from another means it gets out of it, so the letter is removed

parts.note: a lay-off is a temporary suspension of workers from their jobs
a, the indefinite article, means one

explanation.surface: A firm's cash pays the bill, so someone avoids being laid off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'escapes' removes the A from LAYOFF, leaving LYOFF at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone well enough provided with money that they live in ease is said to be well off in this way.

clue.text: Science degree (Cantab.) openly prepared lad

parts.note: Cantab. signals Cambridge, and CU is Cambridge University
BSc is a Bachelor of Science degree
out means openly, as in someone who is out about their identity

explanation.surface: A boy has been readied by a Cambridge science graduate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Be prepared' is the scouting motto, hence the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A junior member of the scouting movement, whose motto is 'Be prepared', is a young boy readied for anything.

clue.text: Mike has name written up in aidememoire

indicators.note: one thing having another means it holds it inside

parts.note: mic is short for microphone, often spelt mike

indicators.note: in a down entry writing upwards reverses the letters of the word for name

parts.note: nomen is the Latin word for name, used for a Roman family name

explanation.surface: A man called Mike gets his name written up in a memory aid.
explanation.walkthrough: Mike is the microphone here, not the NATO-alphabet M; 'written up' turns the Latin word for name upward inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A memory device such as a rhyme or acronym is an aide-memoire, a prompt for recall.

clue.text: Explorer of history first to occupy a rising group of students

indicators.note: the first letter of the word occupy is what is taken
in a down entry rising means the word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: a set is a group of pupils taught together by ability

explanation.surface: A historical explorer is the first to occupy an advancing class of students.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns SET into TES; Lawrence Oates was the explorer on Scott's fatal Antarctic expedition.
explanation.definitionFit: Captain Lawrence Oates was a polar explorer who died on Scott's 1912 Antarctic expedition, so he belongs to history.

clue.text: Curiously make bet holding gems that's hard to understand

indicators.note: the clue words are to be curiously made into something else, a signal to rearrange them

explanation.surface: Oddly placing a wager that contains jewels is baffling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curiously make' rearranges BET HOLDING GEMS into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an exclamation said of something incredible or baffling, beyond easy comprehension.

clue.text: Contribution to court settlement that favours receiver

definitions.text: Contribution to court settlement that favours receiver

parts.words: Contribution to court settlement that favours receiver
parts.note: the legal reading of court and settlement hides a tennis court, where winning against the server helps settle a set

explanation.surface: Something in a legal settlement benefits the person receiving payment.
explanation.walkthrough: The court is a tennis court and the receiver is the player returning serve; winning a game against the server helps settle the set.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis, winning a game while the opponent serves is the classic gain for the receiving player.

clue.text: Object of first snog one has, long fumbles within?

indicators.note: the scrambled word goes inside the phrase for one has

parts.note: you've means one has, using you as the impersonal pronoun

indicators.note: fumbles suggests clumsy handling, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone's first kiss involves a long clumsy grope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one has' as YOU'VE is the impersonal pronoun with a contracted verb, easy to read past as mere surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A teenage sweetheart, the person you first kiss, is the classic object of youthful romance.

clue.text: See 1
I'm surprised by email, but not half as much by text

definitions.text: I'm surprised by email, but not half as much by text

parts.words: I'm surprised by email, but not half as much by text
parts.note: the exclamation of surprise is written out in full in an email but shortened to its three-letter initials in a text message, half the length

explanation.surface: Someone is surprised by an email, though less so by a text message.
explanation.walkthrough: In text messages the exclamation is shortened to OMG, three letters, half the six letters of the spelt-out form.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a casual spelling of 'oh my God', an exclamation of astonishment.

clue.text: What I do should stiffen certain limit?

definitions.text: What I do should stiffen certain limit?

indicators.note: the words stiffen certain limit, or enclose, the run of letters hidden across them

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether their activity ought to tighten some boundary.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits inside 'stiFFEN CERtain'; read as a whole, the speaker who fences sets limits and stiffens them.
explanation.definitionFit: One who fences either puts up boundaries or duels with a foil, and both senses fit the speaker's activity.

clue.text: In nonsense bong tree sits very large bird

indicators.note: one thing sitting in another means it goes inside it
a nod to Edward Lear's nonsense verse, and a signal that the letters are scrambled

parts.note: OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize

explanation.surface: In Lear's nonsense poem, a huge bird perches in the Bong-tree.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bong-tree comes from Edward Lear's nonsense poem 'The Owl and the Pussy-cat'; 'nonsense' rearranges BONG TREE and OS 'sits' in it.
explanation.definitionFit: This dark wild goose of northern coasts is a waterbird of the Arctic and European estuaries.

clue.text: "Off with her head!" — order for exit, on cue

indicators.note: putting the words in a new order calls for their letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: The Queen of Hearts' cry is an instruction to leave the stage on cue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order for' rearranges EXIT ON CUE; the definition is the Queen of Hearts' famous command in Alice in Wonderland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Queen's cry demands a beheading, which is a capital punishment carried out on the condemned.

clue.text: Spooner has to block young female member of consumer association

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the starts of the two pieces change places

parts.note: to stop something is to block it
chick is slang for a young woman

explanation.surface: A girl is barred from joining a consumer rights group.
explanation.walkthrough: The consumer association is a pair of eating utensils: each is a member of the pair, and the user is a consumer of food.
explanation.definitionFit: Each of a pair of eating sticks is one member of the pair that a diner uses together.

clue.text: See 9
Recall curses in university dancing outfit

indicators.note: to recall is to call back, so the run of words is read backwards

parts.note: drat is a mild curse

explanation.surface: A dancer's costume brings back memories of swearing at college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recall' reverses all three pieces at once, so U ends up at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-piece close-fitting garment worn by dancers and gymnasts is a dancing outfit.

clue.text: In Quest for Promise: the Epilogue

parts.note: to be after something is to be in quest of it
your word is your promise

explanation.surface: The final section of a book called In Quest for Promise.
explanation.definitionFit: A closing section added at the end of a book is an epilogue.

clue.text: Extraordinarily fab motor journey?

indicators.note: extraordinarily, read as out of the ordinary, tells you to put the letters in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A wonderful drive in a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extraordinarily' rearranges FAB MOTOR; the question mark marks the definition as a description, since the phrase describes a trip between two points.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting from one place to another is the basic idea of a trip, a journey of any kind.

clue.text: Myriad items off the back of a lorry?

definitions.meaning: a great number, a huge quantity

definitions.text: items off the back of a lorry?
definitions.meaning: a load shed from a lorry, the goods that fall off the back, with a nod to stolen goods

explanation.definitionFit: The informal word means a large amount, and literally names a lorry's load dropped onto the road.

clue.text: Provider of North American muscle?

indicators.note: the letters provide the material for a new word when rearranged

explanation.surface: Who supplies strength to North America?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Provider of' rearranges N, A and MUSCLE; the figure of the US government provides the nation's military power.
explanation.definitionFit: The personification of the US government recruits and pays for America's armed forces, its muscle.

clue.text: See 15
See 4
Fry chicken after rejecting cats?

indicators.note: the bird's word comes after the turned piece
rejecting suggests throwing back, so the word for cats is turned round

parts.note: cats are pets
a hen is a chicken

explanation.surface: Should one cook chicken after spurning the cats' food?
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejecting' turns PETS into STEP. Fry is the British comedian and writer Stephen Fry.
explanation.definitionFit: Stephen Fry is the English actor and broadcaster, so his forename completes the surname.

clue.text: See 5
Wells rising in the heart of a supporter of Kabul

indicators.note: a piece placed in the heart of another goes inside it

parts.note: a fan supports a team

indicators.note: in a down entry rising reads the letters upward

parts.note: H. G. Wells, known by his initials HG

explanation.surface: Wells spring up in the middle of a Kabul football fan's land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns HG into GH.
explanation.definitionFit: Kabul is the capital of Afghanistan, so anything from there carries the national adjective.

clue.text: Do so like non-clergymen from the south

indicators.note: in a down entry, reading from the south means from the bottom up

parts.note: laic means lay, of people who are not clergy

explanation.surface: Act in the manner of laypeople, from a southern point of view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the south' turns LAIC into CIAL. 'Do' is a noun, a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A do is a party or gathering, and so is the noun meaning a festive get-together.

clue.text: Such nightclub acts are on the level

definitions.text: Such nightclub acts are on the level

parts.words: Such nightclub acts are on the level
parts.note: on the level suggests honest, but the acts literally take place on the dance ... rather than a stage

explanation.surface: Nightclub entertainment is honest and above board.
explanation.definitionFit: Cabaret entertainment staged on the dance floor of a club, not a raised stage, is exactly this kind of act.

clue.text: Recoiling, a pearl-seeker comes across part of a raft, he writes

indicators.note: to recoil is to spring back, so the whole assembled run reads backwards
the diver comes across, meeting the log by sitting between its letters

parts.note: a log is one of the timbers lashed into a raft
a pearl diver searches the seabed for oysters

explanation.surface: A pearl diver backs away from a piece of raft, writes someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recoiling' turns the whole assembled container around, not just the diver. Gore Vidal was an American novelist and essayist.
explanation.definitionFit: Gore Vidal was a prolific American novelist and essayist, so he is a man who writes.

clue.text: The prospect of recidivist activity

indicators.note: the run of letters is taken of, or out of, the words that follow

explanation.surface: The likelihood of a criminal reoffending.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'recidiVIST Activity'.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide view, such as a landscape seen from a height, is a prospect.

clue.text: The masses from which I take a vote in state of Ohio

indicators.note: the pieces go inside the scrambled state name
a state can be a disordered condition, so the letters are in a state

parts.note: to poll is to take a vote

explanation.surface: Ordinary people from whom one gathers opinions in Ohio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'state of' rearranges OHIO into HOOI, and I POLL goes 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek phrase means the many, the common people, the masses.

clue.text: See 23
Soldier on manoeuvres underlined maps

indicators.note: military manoeuvres move troops about, a signal to move the letters about

explanation.surface: A soldier on exercises marks up his maps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manoeuvres' rearranges UNDERLINED MAPS. The answer is Latin for 'never despair', urging someone to keep going.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin motto means never despair, the same encouragement as to keep going stubbornly.
